## Research question

How can automated testing find the bugs and security flaws that today only human experts uncover, including silent failures that never crash, without burying developers in false alarms? A central difficulty is the test oracle problem: a test has to know what the right answer should have been.

## Research, in three steps

- Study 1, Coverage-Free Fuzzing (FORGE 2027, under review): an AI model wrote test-input generators for a program it could not see inside. On cJSON, accepted inputs rose from 58% to 97%. A comparison planned in advance reached 93% with no feedback, so most of the gain came from the AI's own generators. Lesson: counting failures is not enough, the AI needs to know which inputs failed and why. Preprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22556342
- Study 2, Beyond Sanitizers (AST 2027, under review): the same inputs were given to the four most common ways Dart apps read JSON, flagging every input where results differed. The AI fuzzer first reached 2.9% against 22.2% for a simple generator, then 28.8% after four short notes about the libraries. Found silent data loss in Google's json_serializable and built_value, both now documented. Preprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22555794
- Study 3, Where Does an LLM Fuzzer's Domain Knowledge Come From? (ICST 2027, under review): compared knowledge written by a person, read from library code, or learned by an agent's own experiments, across eight JSON decoders in Dart and Kotlin, with the study plan published in advance. In Dart, human-written notes worked best (30.9% vs. 11.6% from code and 1.5% with none). In Kotlin, the agent's experiments raised the rate from 50% to 67%. Lesson: an agent only learns from failures it manages to trigger and misses rare ones. Preprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23002933

## Planned Ph.D. directions

- Telling a real bug from intended behavior, and backing each report with evidence a maintainer can check.
- Finding what quietly changes when an app updates a library it depends on.
- Testing tools that do part of a security expert's work and report what they could not check.

## Real-world impact

- Google json_serializable: found that it silently caps out-of-range numbers and turns 1.9 into 1. He reported it with a proposed fix (https://github.com/google/json_serializable.dart/issues/1591) and wrote the fix, which a Google maintainer merged the same day and called a "great fix to a VERY nuanced problem": https://github.com/google/json_serializable.dart/pull/1592. json_serializable is a Google-published Flutter Favorite with 4M+ downloads a month: https://pub.dev/packages/json_serializable
- Google built_value: a missing required list silently becomes empty, now documented: https://github.com/dart-lang/build/pull/5178
- JetBrains kotlinx.serialization: strict mode accepts characters the JSON standard forbids: https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3276
- intercom_flutter: fixed an iOS startup crash in a package with 320K+ monthly downloads: https://github.com/deepak786/intercom_flutter/pull/431
- LLVM: added a controlled comparison to an AddressSanitizer hang report on macOS, showing upstream LLVM 23.1.0 unaffected: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/200447
